title: Factorization of a polynomial with constant term one into linear factors $1-\alpha_jT$ over an algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate, and let $L$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] together with a ring homomorphism $\iota:K\to L$ (for instance $K=\Ql$ and $L=\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\Ql$). Let $P(T)\in K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] satisfy $P(0)=1$, and put $r=\deg P\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Write $P_L\in L[T]$ for the polynomial obtained by applying $\iota$ to the coefficients of $P$, so that $P(x)=P_L(x)$ for $x\in L$ [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Then:

1. Every root $\beta\in L$ of $P$ is nonzero. Hence $\beta\mapsto\beta^{-1}$ is a bijection from the set of roots of $P$ in $L$ onto the set of *reciprocal roots* of $P$ in $L$, the elements $\alpha\in L^\times$ with $P(\alpha^{-1})=0$.

2. There exist $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\in L^\times$ such that, in $L[T]$,

$$
P_L(T)=\prod_{j=1}^{r}(1-\alpha_jT).
$$

3. The family $(\alpha_j)_{1\leq j\leq r}$ is unique up to reordering: for every $\alpha\in L^\times$ the number of indices $j$ with $\alpha_j=\alpha$ equals $m_{\alpha^{-1}}(P_L)$, the multiplicity of $\alpha^{-1}$ as a root of $P_L$ [def-weil-root-multiplicity], which is also the multiplicity $m_\alpha(P_L^\#)$ of $\alpha$ as a root of the reciprocal polynomial $P_L^\#(U)=U^rP_L(U^{-1})$ [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial]. In particular the $\alpha_j$ are exactly the reciprocal roots of $P$ in $L$, each occurring $m_{\alpha_j^{-1}}(P_L)$ times (its *algebraic multiplicity* as a reciprocal root), and the number of reciprocal roots counted with multiplicity is $r=\deg P$.

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: Mathlib factors a polynomial over an algebraically closed field as leadingCoeff · ∏ (X - β) over its roots (Splits.eq_prod_roots with IsAlgClosed.splits_domain), not as ∏ (1 - α_j X) indexed by the inverses of the roots; turning one into the other (every root is nonzero since the constant term is 1, X - β = -β(1 - β⁻¹X), and the product of the -β equals leadingCoeff⁻¹) is a short argument, not a one-line specialization, so the node is not a leaf
